programme.title: Journey Home, David Gulpilil

programme.title: Vai
programme.desc: Vai is a feature film made by nine female Pacific filmmakers, filmed in seven different Pacific countries - Fiji, Tonga, Solomon Islands, Kuki Airani (Cook Islands), Samoa, Niue and Aotearoa (New Zealand). It is about the journey of empowerment through culture over the lifetime of one woman, Vai, played by a different Indigenous actress in each of the Pacific countries.

programme.title: A United Kingdom
programme.desc: The story of Oxford-educated King Seretse Khama of Botswana and how his loving but controversial marriage to white Englishwoman, Ruth Williams, in 1948 plunged his kingdom into political and diplomatic turmoil. Directed by Amma Asante and stars David Oyelowo and Rosamund Pike.

To escape a harsh existence and return to his home country, a young Afghan cameleer falls in with a mysterious bushman on the run with stolen Crown gold. Directed by Roderick MacKay and stars Ahmed Malick, Baykali Ganambarr and David Wenham.

programme.title: Storm Boy
programme.desc: Mike is a lonely Australian boy living in a coastal wilderness with his reclusive father. In search of friendship, he encounters an Indigenous man estranged from his tribe, and the two form a bond in the care of three orphaned pelican chicks. Stars Peter Cummins, David Gulpilil and Greg Rowe.

programme.desc: Adam arrives in Hainan, ready for the Liaw family reunion. After months apart, he’s meeting his wife and two kids here in Haikou, to join him at the family reunion, but before they arrive, he’s keen to check out the islands food and culture. Hainan Island is known as ‘Oriental Hawaii’, and it enjoys the same palm-fringed golden beaches and tropical climate.
